method: Actual encoded MP4 decoded to all 150 PNGs. Directly inspected 10 labelled contact sheets covering every frame 0..149, then opened frames 40,43,48,51,54,60,72,116 at original 1920x1080 resolution. No continuous normal-speed or slow-motion video playback was viewed in this review.

observations.finding: Upper basket contains visible red/yellow fruit and lower basket is empty; both walls and overlapping fruit occlude some items, so seven cannot be counted individually from this view.

Harvest floor panels separate. The first visible red fruit moves downward through the opening, changes pitch and travels toward the lower front region across frames40..43. It is not a row of fixed-orientation vertical sprites.

Further red/yellow fruit descend with differing orientations. Yellow fruit seen upright/tilted at48 are lying and turned at51..54; red fruit shift left and rotate. The upper basket becomes visually empty, and fruit roll/settle in the lower basket. Some travel is hidden behind the solid upper front wall.
Lower cargo has stable lying fruit and upper basket stays empty. No reappearance of the initial upright red/yellow silhouettes seen in the earlier reset-only probe; frame72 checked full resolution.
Harvest floor closes after the lower fruit visually settle. No visible fruit remain trapped in the upper basket.
Lower top lids close over the settled fruit. Their disappearance from view follows the closing opaque lid edges; this is occlusion, not visible fading.
Lids remain closed, upper basket empty, camera/framing stable. No visible initial-pose ghost or off-screen camera-reset frame appears.

count_interpretation.reason: Opaque basket walls, fruit overlap and final closed lid prevent individual counting. The movie alone does not prove each ID continuously.
count_interpretation.separate_numeric_evidence: ../settings/05_handoff_continuity_evidence.json records the same seven IDs in all151 bake samples with visibility/scale unchanged; offline geometry audit verifies all seven end inside lower cargo.

contact_interpretation: Frame pairs show orientation/trajectory changes and settling consistent with the Bullet contact bake. Visual review does not independently measure contact forces, submillimetre penetration or hidden contact.
result: No blocking visual defect found within all-frame contact-sheet and selected full-resolution-frame scope. Earlier upper-basket ghost not observed in final encoded frames.
limitations: No continuous-video playback claim; temporal smoothness at real playback speed is not independently judged here.
Contact sheets are reduced resolution; selected critical frames were additionally opened full resolution.
Single camera cannot distinguish every occluded individual ID visually; use independent geometry/bake ledger for count continuity.
No real-robot or operational autonomous success claim.
